illustration.alt: The companion under an open umbrella, as the first raindrops fall.

companionLines.bo: Hi {nome}! It's raining. Will you come under the umbrella with me?
companionLines.pilu: Hi {nome}! Can you hear the rain on the window? Tap, tap.
companionLines.tango: Hi {nome}! It's raining! Outside, now! ...Wait. Wellies.

illustration.alt: Emma, with two messy bunches, a yellow coat and red wellies, watches the rain from the window; Grandma holds the umbrella; Pietrolino is on the windowsill.

screens.text: It's raining. The drops tap on the window: tap, tap. Emma puts on her red wellies. Grandma takes the umbrella.

illustration.alt: In the wood the water runs away in a little stream; one drop jumps out towards a flower. Emma watches, Grandma is close by with the umbrella.

screens.text: In the wood the water runs away. But one drop jumps! "Hi! I'm Drop. I want to give the flowers a drink!"

companionLines.bo: A drop that talks! Careful, I'll get wet.
companionLines.pilu: Did you see? Drop is jumping towards the flowers.
companionLines.tango: It jumps like me! ...Wait. Where is it going?

illustration.alt: Three pictures in a row: a cloud, a drop, a flower. Emma and Grandma look at them under the umbrella.

screens.text: Drop goes on a long journey. Emma watches it with Grandma.

companionLines.bo: Let's look at Drop's journey, slowly.
companionLines.pilu: Look carefully: one picture at a time.
companionLines.tango: Three pictures! Come on! ...Wait. One at a time.

lesson.together: Point to one picture at a time and just say: "This is the cloud". Then ask: "Where is the drop?". At the end, point to one and ask: "What is it called?". If they touch a different picture, tell them that one's name, nothing more.
lesson.ask: And this one, what is it called?
lesson.done: The cloud, the drop, the flower. That's Drop's journey.

illustration.alt: A drop jumps onto a flower, then rises up, smaller and smaller, all the way to a cloud. Emma looks up.

screens.text: Plop! Drop jumps onto a flower. The flower drinks. Then Drop goes up, up, all the way to the cloud.

companionLines.bo: Drop is flying up! Will it come back with the rain?
companionLines.pilu: Look: Drop goes all the way up to the cloud.
companionLines.tango: Up, up, up! Faster than me!

illustration.alt: On the balcony at home Emma and Grandma put a bowl out in the rain, next to a plant.

screens.text: At home, Emma and Grandma put a bowl on the balcony. "This one's for the rain," says Emma.

companionLines.bo: Tonight I'll turn off the tap, {nome}.
companionLines.pilu: Tomorrow I'll see if the bowl is full, {nome}.
companionLines.tango: Tonight I'll turn off the tap, quick, {nome}!
